newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU entry risky if not fully ready -Trichet quoted.
newsitem.headline: EMU entry risky if not fully ready -Trichet quoted.

text.p: Countries would act against their own interests if they joined European Economic and Monetary Union before their economies were fully convergent with those of other members, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet was quoted on Thursday as telling a parliamentary committee.
Trichet attended the hearing, of the parliament's finance committee, on Wednesday.

"He said that...France and Germany's interests were the same -- to have a European currency which had the same credibility as those of the best national currencies in Europe, guaranteed by a European central bank, which would be independent and therefore credible, and not a European currency which was based on an average of currencies with unequal credibility, which could lead to an increase in our market interest rates," the minutes quoted him as saying.

"Moreover, he added that it was not in the interests of a country whose economy had not fully converged (with others joining monetary union) to join EMU, thereby depriving itself of possibilities for adjustment," he said.

European Union countries will decide in early 1998 which countries will join the single European currency when it is first launched in 1999, on the basis of economic convergence criteria contained in the Maastricht treaty.
